messages:
Sam - Partnerships: Heads-up — reseller is going live with a promo on the EU marketplace next Wed. They flagged a potential promotional burst: estimate 120k–180k GPU-hours over ~72 hours. Need infra sanity check on IO/egress and a provisioning plan. cc @Maya (infra) @Devon (eng-runtime) :eyes:
Maya (infra): Thanks — can you share the burst shape? total GPU-hours is useful but peak concurrent and sequence length distribution will drive our provisioning and KV cache pressure.
Sam - Partnerships: From their workbook: expected peak concurrency 1.8k–2.2k GPUs, median seq ~512 tokens, 90th pct ~1024. They want high-priority traffic on our dedicated SKU and will ramp clients in staged cohorts.
Devon (eng-runtime): Noted. If seqs are that long KV cache will increase per-request memory significantly. We should estimate memory pressure and whether we need to shift to larger instance types or more nodes.
Leah (finance): Quick question on cost: if we provision capacity for peak vs rely on spot backfill, what's the delta? Need a ballpark to discuss with partner concessions.
Devon (eng-runtime): Rough calc: 2k GPUs * 72h = 144k GPU-hrs. Spot ~ $0.60/hr => ~$86.4k. Reserved/committed amortized ~$0.35/hr => ~$50.4k. Those are compute-only numbers; network egress and storage I/O can add ~15–25% depending on traffic pattern.
Maya (infra): Main operational risk is IO and network egress in eu-west-1. We saw last-year promo in APAC saturate our egress NATs and cause tails. We should run a targeted IO/network probe against the EU cluster and pre-warm caches. Also consider connection churn limits for streaming sessions. :warning:
Maya (infra): Quick probe plan — running a synthetic workload that mirrors partner shape (512 median, 1024 tail). Command to seed probe job:
```
# run 2000 parallel probes with median seq=512
kubectl run probe-burst --image=redwood/probe:latest --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/sh -c "python probe.py --concurrency 2000 --median_seq 512 --duration 10800"
```
Maya (infra): I'll kick that off EOD and post metrics (egress p95/p99, disk iops, CPU, mem pressure) here.
Ops-bot: [job] prewarm/probe created by @Maya — id prewarm-1872468 — status: queued
Tony (sre): I'll subscribe to the job logs and capture NLB connection counts. Suggestion: enforce a soft cap of 60 streaming connections/node and apply token-based admission to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also add a short-lived rate-limiter on the marketplace ingress path for the first 12h of the ramp.
Leah (finance): If we need to reserve additional capacity for the promo window, we should compare 30-day reserved burst vs on-demand/spot. Also confirm whether partner will cover incremental costs or expect included in marketplace agreement.
Sam - Partnerships: Partner is open to a staged ramp (25% first 8h, then 50% next 12h, then full). They asked for SLOs: <200ms for small seqs (<=128) and best-effort for long seqs. They can tolerate occasional fallback to a lower-fidelity model for some cohorts.
Devon (eng-runtime): Good — fallback plan: route long-seq heavy users to a quantized 4-bit variant for first 24h to reduce memory/GPU footprint, while dedicated hosts the highest priority clients. That should reduce upstream IO and caching pressure.
Maya (infra): Action items I have: 1) Run IO/network probe and post results by EOD 2) If probe shows >=80% network/IO utilization, schedule pre-provision of extra NFS/EBS throughput and request transient egress quota with cloud provider 3) Prepare a prewarm fleet of warm containers + warmed KV caches.
Tony (sre): My action items: 1) Temp connection caps and NLB rules before ramp 2) Real-time alerting thresholds for p95/p99 egress and stream latencies 3) Coordinate with on-call for escalation playbook.
Leah (finance): My action: model cost scenarios (spot vs reserve vs hybrid) and share a one-pager for partner negotiation by tomorrow morning.
Sam - Partnerships: I'll confirm the staged ramp schedule with the reseller and ask them to provide hourly expected concurrency during the 72h window. Also negotiate cost-sharing for any emergency reserved capacity.
Maya (infra): If anyone needs the probe command or config, ping me. I'll post the initial metrics here once it's running. If IO looks marginal we'll trigger the quantized fallback earlier. :white_check_mark:
Devon (eng-runtime): Thanks — I'll prepare rollout knobs for automatic fallback to quantized models and add tracing tags so we can correlate QoS with model variant.
Sam - Partnerships: Appreciated. Let's sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC after probe results.
Tony (sre): Adding a quick note — consider pre-creating extra NAT/Egress IPs in the EU region to avoid allocation delays. I've seen allocations take ~20–45min during high cloud demand.
Maya (infra): Good call. I'll request them proactively if probe indicates high egress pressure.
Ops-bot: [note] reminder scheduled: sync meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC (participants: Sam, Maya, Devon, Leah, Tony)
